title: Viscohypoplastic bentonite (VIBE, Mašín2026)
summary: VIBE describes how swelling-clay microstructure, larger pores, temperature and elapsed time combine to change stress and water retention.
introduction: The double-structure description separates swelling within clay aggregates from deformation of the pores between them. Its updated implementation adds a time-dependent contribution to stress response and allows thermal and hydraulic changes to affect the two structures differently.

behaviours.title: Relaxation during a hold
behaviours.explanation: With viscosity enabled, holding total strain, suction and temperature fixed can still change stress because elapsed physical time remains part of the law.

behaviours.title: Hydraulic and thermal coupling
behaviours.explanation: Changing suction alters water held in the larger pores and the swelling of the finer structure. Temperature affects retention and the microstructural response; the 2026 formulation must be distinguished from its earlier rate-independent predecessors.

parameterNote: Material parameters govern compression, unloading, swelling, water retention and time-dependent stress response. No laboratory parameter editor or calibrated example is provided for this reading profile.
preparation: A prepared state requires initial stress, void ratio, suction, absolute temperature and the hydraulic branch. Empty placeholder internal variables in the author driver are filled by its separate initialization routine; they are not a physically prepared specimen.
scope: This is a reading profile for the exact2026 VIBE publication. A public laboratory run is unavailable. The inspected implementation evolves net stress with physical time and thermal/hydraulic controls.
limits: The formulation couples prescribed thermal and hydraulic histories to local material response; it does not by itself solve heat transfer, water flow or repository-scale boundary-value problems. Parameters and preparation must match the selected bentonite and experimental protocol.
